children: Earnings season continues with 14 companies reporting quarterly results across communication services, consumer discretionary, consumer staples, and information technology.
Out of the 14 companies reporting, 11 exceeded EPS expectations, while 3 came in-line. Notably, 12 firms posted year-over-year earnings growth.
Out of the 14 companies reporting, 12 exceeded revenue expectations, while 2 fell below analyst estimates. Notably, all 14 firms posted year-over-year revenue growth.
Let’s take a look at some of the companies that reported earnings this week:

, with adjusted EPS of $1.77 (vs. $1.68 consensus) and revenue rising 16% Y/Y to $25.95B (vs. $25.2B est.). For FY27, Disney guided for double-digit adjusted EPS growth and ~8% segment operating income growth (ex-53rd week), while raising its annual dividend by 33% to $2.00/share.

, with adjusted EPS of $3.86 (vs. $3.84 consensus) and revenue rising 4.9% Y/Y to $43.4B on 2.2% comparable sales growth. Management projected ~4.5% FY26 sales growth and 2.0% EPS growth, while naming CFO Richard McPhail to succeed Ted Decker as CEO effective November 23.

, with non-GAAP EPS of $3.10 (vs. $2.90 consensus) and comparable sales rising 1.8% (vs. +0.4% est.) on a 17.4% jump in online sales. Management guided full-year sales to ~$92.5B (vs. $92.1B consensus) and adjusted EPS to $12.25 (vs. $12.27 est.), with comparable sales seen flat to +0.5%.

jumped 8.05% post-earnings after Q3 revenue rose 5.5% Y/Y to $15.95B on 4% comparable sales growth (beating the +3.8% consensus), while non-GAAP EPS of $1.34 matched estimates. Management guided full-year comp sales growth to 4% and EPS to $5.17–$5.20 (vs. $5.23 consensus), alongside plans to buy back ~$3.0B in stock during FY27.

shares rose 4.01% post-earnings after a Q3 beat-and-raise, as tariff-refund tailwinds ($0.50/share) and <1% average ticket growth overshadowed 5.6% comparable sales growth (vs. 3.61% estimates) and adjusted EPS of $2.65 (vs. $2.08 estimates). Management raised FY26 guidance to ~6% sales growth ($111B) and adjusted EPS of $10.65–$11.40, while lifting capex to $5B–$6B.

jumped 8.72% post-earnings despite a 47% Y/Y drop in FQ4 adjusted EPS to $0.61 (vs. $0.62 consensus) as reported revenue rose 5.2% to $14.59B (-4.0% comparable). Deeper beef losses ($171M) and tighter chicken margins (8.7% vs. 12.7%) weighed on profits, while management projected FY27 sales to decline 3.5%–5.5% with $1.7B–$2.15B in adjusted operating income.

slipped 1.04% post-earnings despite beating Q3 estimates, as a cautious holiday outlook tempered results. Adjusted EPS of $0.65 topped the $0.64 consensus, while U.S. comparable sales rose 2.9% (vs. 2.8% estimates) on a 23% jump in U.S. e-commerce; management guided FY27 revenue growth to 4.9%–5.2% and EPS to $2.84–$2.89 (midpoint $2.865 vs. $2.89 estimates).

surged 6.42% post-earnings after an FQ1 FY27 beat-and-raise, with adjusted EPS of $1.05 (vs. $0.97 consensus) and revenue rising 39% Y/Y to $3.45B (vs. $3.31B est.). Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to $14.52B–$14.57B and adjusted EPS to $4.26–$4.30 (vs. $4.18 estimates), alongside announcing a $4.5B all-stock deal to acquire Applied Compute.

shares fell 2.89% post-earnings after delivering a strong Q3 beat-and-raise, reporting adjusted EPS of $2.68 (beating consensus by $0.21) and revenue surging 103.2% Y/Y to $115.84B ($7.13B above forecasts). Management guided Q4 revenue to ~$130B (±3%, vs. $124.89B estimates) and lifted FY28 revenue growth expectations to ~75% Y/Y, while noting it could exhaust its remaining $227.3B share buyback authorization by FY28.

plunged ~12.8% post-earnings as soft guidance overshadowed a Q1 FY27 beat, with revenue up 12% Y/Y to $4.4B and non-GAAP EPS of $2.91 topping the $2.64 consensus. Amid Credit Karma softness, management guided Q2 revenue to $4.93B–$4.95B (vs. $5.11B estimates) and non-GAAP EPS to $3.17–$3.22 (vs. $3.94 estimates), while affirming FY27 non-GAAP EPS of $22.88–$23.12 (vs. $23.81 estimates). Intuit also agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons, acquired AI platform Sequence, and declared a $1.38/share quarterly dividend.

shares fell 7.1% post-earnings after a Q4 beat-and-raise, with adjusted EPS of $3.61 (vs. $3.37 consensus) and revenue jumping 41% Y/Y to $1.99B (vs. $1.95B estimates). For Q1 FY27, management guided adjusted EPS to $3.63–$3.69 (vs. $3.21 estimates) and revenue to $2.04B–$2.06B (vs. $1.96B estimates).
